goal: Reduce filler words, especially when put on the spot.
userTurn: My ums go through the roof the second someone puts me on the spot. How do I fix that?
emotionalSignal: practical, a bit self-critical — genuinely wants a mechanism, not comfort

recentReps.note: fillers tripled the moment the timer pressure landed vs his calm baseline of 3

caseFormulation.hypothesis: fillers are a stalling reflex — he starts the sentence before he knows where it's going, then fills the gap

expectedCoachMove: Reframe fillers as a timing reflex, not a vocabulary problem — coach the PAUSE as the replacement (hold a silent beat instead of filling). Cite his own split (3 calm vs 9 under pressure) so it's diagnostic. One concrete move: the silent-beat swap. Must coach the pause, NOT tell him to close his mouth/lips or 'stop saying um'. Frame as a test.
badAnswerExample: Just slow down and think before you speak. Close your mouth when you feel an um coming. Practice more and be more confident — the ums will naturally go away once you work on your confidence.
excellentAnswerExample: That spike is timing, not vocabulary — calm you sits at 3 fillers; put on the spot you hit 9. The um is you starting the sentence before you know the end of it. So swap the um for a silent beat: when the question lands, hold one second, pick your first word, then go. Try it next Sudden Death rep — one held beat before each answer. That tests whether the pause can do the job the um was doing.
